group: Group C (Civil and Mechanical Engineering, Semester S1)

checks.title: Mathematics for Electrical Science and Physical Science - 1

findings.issue: Confirmed mismatch: GYMAT101 is the official S1 mathematics course for Group C (Civil & Mechanical), and complete notes plus a matching syllabus reader exist in the repo, but the catalog omits GYMAT101 entirely for 'civil' and 'me' branches.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 3: 'SEMESTER S1 / MATHEMATICS FOR ELECTRICAL SCIENCE AND PHYSICAL SCIENCE - 1 / (Groups B & C) / Course Code GYMAT101'. PDF pp. 3-4: Modules 1-4.
findings.repo_evidence: src/data/notes.ts: sharedS1Subjects(branchId) wraps the GYMAT101 entry in `...(branchId === 'ece' || branchId === 'eee' ? [...] : [])`, excluding 'civil' and 'me'. Notes in electrical-maths-module-1..4 and courses.GYMAT101 in src/features/syllabi/cse.ts cover all 4 modules accurately.

checks.title: Physics for Physical Science and Life Science

findings.issue: Confirmed missing course: Official Group C S1/S2 Physics course GZPHT121 has no mapped note directories, no syllabus reader definition, and no catalog entry under Civil or Mechanical S1.
findings.source_evidence: PDF pp. 8-10: 'SEMESTER S1/S2 / PHYSICS FOR PHYSICAL SCIENCE AND LIFE SCIENCE (Groups C & D) / Course Code GZPHT121' covering Module 1 (Laser & Fibre Optics), Module 2 (Interference and Diffraction), Module 3 (Quantum Mechanics), Module 4 (Waves & Acoustics).
findings.repo_evidence: No mapped note directories for GZPHT121; src/features/syllabi/cse.ts only defines GAPHT121; src/data/notes.ts only adds Physics (GBPHT121) for 'ece' and 'eee', leaving 'civil' and 'me' with no Physics entry.

missing_topics: Module 1: Laser & Fibre Optics (Ruby, CO2, semiconductor lasers, numerical aperture, fibre optic communication)
Module 2: Interference and Diffraction (Cosine law, thin films, Newton's rings, air wedge, single slit, grating)
Module 3: Quantum Mechanics (Uncertainty principle, Schrodinger equations, 1D box, quantum tunnelling)
Module 4: Waves & Acoustics (Stretched string vibrations, reverberation, Sabine's formula, ultrasonics, NDT, SONAR)

checks.title: Chemistry for Physical Science

findings.issue: Confirmed missing syllabus reader: GCCYT122 is missing from the syllabus reader definitions, and syllabusHref is explicitly disabled (undefined) for 'civil' and 'me' in the catalog.
findings.source_evidence: PDF pp. 17-19: 'SEMESTER S1/S2 / CHEMISTRY FOR PHYSICAL SCIENCE (Group C) / Course Code GCCYT122'.
findings.repo_evidence: src/features/syllabi/cse.ts defines GXCYT122 (Group A/B Chemistry) but not GCCYT122. src/data/notes.ts sets `syllabusHref: branchId === 'civil' || branchId === 'me' ? undefined : ...` and titles the course 'Engineering Chemistry' instead of 'Chemistry for Physical Science'.

findings.issue: Possible gap in Module 1 notes: Solid and semisolid lubricants classification and supercapacitor materials in nanomaterials are not clearly evidenced in the Module 1 note outline.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 18, Module 1: 'Lubricants: Classification - Solid, Semisolid and Liquid lubricants' and 'Nanomaterials: ... Applications of nanomaterials – Supercapacitor Materials'.
findings.repo_evidence: chemistry-civil-mech-module-1/notes.md p. 7 (L341-L412) lists 'Classification of Greases' and 'Liquid Lubricants' without an explicit solid lubricants heading; p. 11 (L768) lists 'Applications of Nanomaterials' without explicitly highlighting supercapacitor materials.

findings.issue: Possible gap in Module 2 notes: Nernst equation for single electrode and cell (and numerical problems) is not explicitly shown in the Module 2 section headings.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 18, Module 2: 'Electrochemical Cell- Electrode potential- Nernst equation for single electrode and cell (Numerical problems)'.
findings.repo_evidence: chemistry-civil-mech-module-2/notes.md pp. 2-4 (L21-L300) covers Daniell cell, reference electrodes, and electrochemical series applications (equilibrium constant/feasibility), without a dedicated Nernst equation heading.

findings.issue: Possible gap in Module 3 notes: Beer-Lambert's law (and numericals), role of conjugation in electronic spectroscopy, DTA of CaC2O4.H2O, and GC exhaust gas analysis are not explicitly surfaced in headings.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 19, Module 3: 'Beer Lambert’s law – Numerical problems', 'Role of Conjugation in absorption maxima', 'DTA of CaC2O4.H2O', 'Analysis of chemical composition of exhaust gases'.
findings.repo_evidence: chemistry-civil-mech-module-3/notes.md p. 2-3 (L20-L179) has 'Worked Example' and 'UV-Visible Spectroscopy Fundamentals'; p. 5 (L310, L354-L383) explicitly lists 'Thermogram of Calcium Oxalate Monohydrate' under TGA but not under DTA; p. 6 (L446) lists general 'Applications of Gas Chromatography'.

missing_topics: Module 1: Solid lubricants (possible gap in outline)
Module 1: Supercapacitor materials under nanomaterials (possible gap in outline)
Module 2: Nernst equation for single electrode and cell and numerical problems (possible gap in outline)
Module 3: Beer-Lambert's law and numerical problems, Role of conjugation in absorption maxima (possible gap in outline)
Module 3: DTA of CaC2O4.H2O and GC analysis of exhaust gases (possible gap in outline)

checks.title: Engineering Mechanics

findings.issue: Confirmed missing course & wrong course in catalog: Group C S1 requires GCEST103 (Engineering Mechanics), which has no notes, no syllabus reader, and no catalog entry. Instead, the catalog lists GMEST103 (Engineering Graphics) in S1 for Civil and Mechanical.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 26: 'SEMESTER S1 / ENGINEERING MECHANICS / Course Code GCEST103' (Modules 1-4: Statics/Force systems, Friction/Centroid/Moment of inertia, Rectilinear translation/D'Alembert's principle, Curvilinear translation/Projectile/Rotation). PDF p. 95 shows Engineering Graphics for Group C is S2 course GCEST203 (which includes Tetrahedron and Frustum, unlike GMEST103).
findings.repo_evidence: src/data/notes.ts: sharedS1Subjects assigns GMEST103 ('Engineering Graphics and Computer Aided Drawing') with `modules: []` to 'civil' and 'me' in S1. GCEST103 is absent from both src/data/notes.ts and src/features/syllabi/cse.ts.

missing_topics: Module 1: Introduction to statics, forces in space, support reactions of beams (point load and UDL), 2D and 3D force systems, moment, couple, resultants, free-body diagram and 2D/3D equilibrium
Module 2: Friction (laws, blocks and ladder), Centroid of composite areas, Moment of inertia (parallel/perpendicular axis theorems, polar MOI, radius of gyration, mass MOI of ring and disc)
Module 3: Dynamics - rectilinear translation, kinematics and kinetics equations of motion, D'Alembert's principle, motion on horizontal/inclined surfaces, connected bodies
Module 4: Curvilinear translation, differential equations of projectile motion, kinematics of rotation, rotation of rigid body about fixed axis under constant moment
extra_or_wrong_topics: Catalog and syllabus reader expose GMEST103 (Group A/B Engineering Graphics) in S1 instead of GCEST103 (Engineering Mechanics)

checks.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering & Civil Engineering

findings.issue: Confirmed missing course & wrong course in catalog: Group C S1 requires GCEST104 (Introduction to Mechanical Engineering & Civil Engineering), which has no notes, no syllabus reader, and no catalog entry. Instead, the catalog lists GXEST104 (Introduction to Electrical and Electronics Engineering) in S1 for Civil and Mechanical.
findings.source_evidence: PDF pp. 30-32: 'SEMESTER S1 / INTRODUCTION TO MECHANICAL ENGINEERING & CIVIL ENGINEERING / Course Code GCEST104'. (In Group C, Basic Electrical & Electronics Engineering is S2 course GZEST204 on PDF p. 99, which also differs in syllabus from GXEST104).
findings.repo_evidence: src/data/notes.ts: sharedS1Subjects assigns GXEST104 ('Introduction to Electrical and Electronics Engineering') with `modules: []` to 'civil' and 'me' in S1. GCEST104 is completely absent from src/data/notes.ts and src/features/syllabi/cse.ts.

missing_topics: Module 1: Thermodynamic cycles (Carnot, Otto, Diesel), IC Engines (CI, SI, 2-stroke, 4-stroke, CRDI, MPFI, hybrid), Refrigeration (reversed Carnot, vapour compression) & Psychrometry, Central AC layout

Module 2: Pumps (Reciprocating, Centrifugal) & Hydraulic Turbines, Power transmission (gears, clutches, bearings), Manufacturing (casting, forging, rolling, extrusion, welding, soldering, brazing, machining, CNC, 3D printing)

Module 3: Civil Engineering disciplines, NBC occupancy types, load/non-load bearing structures, residential building components and site selection, KBR area definitions (built-up, plinth, floor, carpet, FAR), relevance of NBC/KBR/CRZ

Module 4: Conventional construction materials (brick, stone, sand, cement, timber), Cement concrete & IS tests (slump, cube compressive strength), Structural steel & reinforcements, Soil origin and weathering
extra_or_wrong_topics: Catalog and syllabus reader expose GXEST104 (Group A/B Introduction to Electrical and Electronics Engineering) in S1 instead of GCEST104 (Introduction to Mechanical Engineering & Civil Engineering)

checks.title: Algorithmic Thinking with Python

findings.issue: Confirmed catalog linkage bug: Although UCEST105 is in the catalog for 'civil' and 'me' and shared Python notes exist in the repo, the catalog sets `modules: []` for 'civil' and 'me', hiding all four note modules from Group C students.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 37: 'SEMESTER S1 / ALGORITHMIC THINKING WITH PYTHON / (Common to All Branches) / Course Code UCEST105'.
findings.repo_evidence: src/data/notes.ts: In sharedS1Subjects, UCEST105 sets `modules: branchId === 'ece' || branchId === 'eee' ? [...] : []`, leaving 'civil' and 'me' with an empty module list.

findings.issue: Confirmed missing topic in Module 3 notes: Recursion (definition, call stack, avoiding circularity, and recursive sample problems) is completely absent from python-module-3/notes.md.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 38, Module 3: 'RECURSION:- Recursion Defined, Reasons for using Recursion, The Call Stack, Recursion and the Stack, Avoiding Circularity in Recursion, Sample problems - Finding the nth Fibonacci number, greatest common divisor of two positive integers, the factorial of a positive integer, adding two positive integers, the sum of digits of a positive number'.
findings.repo_evidence: python-module-3/notes.md (pp. 1-29, L1-L1054) covers selection, loops, functions, strings, lists, tuples, NumPy arrays, sets, and dictionaries, but contains no section or page on Recursion or the Call Stack (only a brief 1-paragraph mention of recursion inside Divide and Conquer in python-module-4/notes.md p. 4 L76).

findings.issue: Confirmed missing/incomplete sample problems in Module 2 & 3 notes: Expression evaluation d=a+b*c, printing numbers 1 to 50 in descending order, largest of n numbers, and merge sort decomposition demonstration are missing or incomplete.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 38, Module 2: '* - Evaluate an expression, d=a+b*c... print the numbers from 1 to 50 in descending order, find the sum of n numbers input by the user (using all the three loop variants)... largest of n numbers'. PDF pp. 38-39, Module 3: 'Functions with multiple return values' and '* The idea should be introduced and demonstrated using Merge sort, the problem of returning the top three integers from a list of n>=3 integers as examples.'
findings.repo_evidence: python-module-2/notes.md omits d=a+b*c, descending 1 to 50, and largest of n numbers (and spills Python `range()`, `if/elif`, lists, and NumPy arrays into Module 2 pp. 44-50). python-module-3/notes.md p. 20 (L686) demonstrates returning the top 3 largest values in a list, but omits Merge sort in Module 3 (covered only in Module 4 p. 4 L80) and does not explicitly highlight multiple return values via tuple packing.

findings.issue: Confirmed syllabus reader module boundary mismatch: src/features/syllabi/cse.ts places Module 3's 'SELECTION AND ITERATION USING PYTHON', 'Sequence data types in Python', and 'Numpy library' into Module 2 of the syllabus reader.
findings.source_evidence: PDF p. 38: Module 2 covers only 'ALGORITHM AND PSEUDOCODE REPRESENTATION' and 'FLOWCHARTS'. Module 3 begins with 'SELECTION AND ITERATION USING PYTHON:- if-else, elif, for loop, range, while loop. Sequence data types in Python - list, tuple, set, strings, dictionary, Creating and using Arrays in Python (using Numpy library).'
findings.repo_evidence: src/features/syllabi/cse.ts: courses.UCEST105.modules[1] ('Module 2: Algorithms, flowcharts and control flow') includes `{ title: 'Selection, iteration and collections', subtopics: ['if, elif, for, range and while', 'Lists, tuples, sets, strings and dictionaries', 'Arrays using NumPy'] }`, which belongs to Module 3.

missing_topics: Module 2: Sample problems - Evaluate expression d=a+b*c, print numbers from 1 to 50 in descending order, largest of n numbers
Module 3: Recursion - definition, reasons for using recursion, the call stack, recursion and the stack, avoiding circularity in recursion
Module 3: Recursion sample problems - nth Fibonacci number, GCD of two positive integers, factorial, adding two positive integers, sum of digits of a positive number
Module 3: Problem decomposition demonstrated using Merge sort, and explicit coverage of functions with multiple return values
extra_or_wrong_topics: Syllabus reader (src/features/syllabi/cse.ts) places Module 3 topics (Python selection/iteration, sequence data types, NumPy arrays) into Module 2
python-module-2/notes.md (pp. 44-50) includes Python range(), if/elif, quadratic solver, list slicing, and NumPy arrays which belong to Module 3

catalogue_findings.evidence: PDF p. 8 (GZPHT121 for Groups C & D); src/data/notes.ts lines 101-110 (only adds GBPHT121 for ECE/EEE; Civil/ME get no Physics subject).
